applied.summary: P0.9 (11th KEEP file) was entirely absent from the repoint set. Verified live: p0-9-hindsight-banks-mulch.md:198 names P1.6 (mulch-priming consumer contract) and :218 names P1.1 (JSON-RPC error-code range allocation) — both forward-looking, both requiring repoint. AC1's grep was scoped to phase-1 only while the E2E Slice and DoD both asserted zero retired IDs across 'the 11 KEEP files', so the story shipped a DoD that was false as scripted. Added the P0.9 row to the amendment A table (198→DF1.6, 218→DF3.1), widened AC1's grep to include phase-0/stories/p0-{5,9}, added P0.9 to Files to Modify, corrected marker-set count 10→11 amended files in E2E Slice + DoD, and occurrence-table count eight→nine files.

Undiscovered shared_pattern_note contradiction in the KEEP corpus: p1-14-outcome-record-router.md names costCents at :30 (AC1), :37 (schema), :40 (guards), contradicting DD-9 (integer micro-dollars, never costCents). DD-9 names only P1.13 (RE-DERIVE→DF2.8), so nothing else in the slate catches the KEEP-side instance. A field name inside an AC is AC substance, so INV-1 forbids the edit — recorded in amendment B under the existing 'record, do not invent' mechanism, with the disposition that DF2.8 restates the cap as 5,000,000 µ$. INV-3 and the Observability Contract updated to include the drift record.
AC1's Given clause said 'the ten amendments in §Technical Notes' — there are five amendments (A–E) across (now) eleven files. Corrected to 'amendments A–E'.

AC1 (make-or-break) attributed the push to the tier-3 team — 'the tier-3 team reads the comment, implements a fix, and pushes to the PR branch' — then contradicted itself in a trailing parenthetical. That directly contradicts the story's own INV-3 (no push credential in a box), D8, and R5 §6 fact 17, and ignores R2 §10's explicit instruction ('under D8 the push is host-side, so this AC must be re-split the same way P1.15's is'). An implementer reading AC1 literally puts a git credential in the box. Re-split: AC1 now covers read-comment + implement-fix with commits reaching the branch in AC2; the push clause is host-side in AC2 only, marked 're-split per R2 §10 ... never in the box, INV-3/D8'.

The middle of the bounded loop had no AC. AC1 covered dispatch, AC3 green, AC4 budget exhaustion after two failures — nothing specified that attempt 2 is dispatched or that it carries attempt 1's diagnostics, despite fixContext.attempt existing in the schema. Extended AC4 with the re-dispatch transition: attempt 2 increments fixContext.attempt and carries attempt 1's CI failure output.

E2E Slice said 'dispatch_task runs lead + one fixer', contradicting the Technical Notes' binding F6 roster ('one write-capable worker, plus a read-only analyst and a verifying lead'). Since the E2E demo is the MANDATORY DoD item and AC5 is the guard on that exact roster shape, corrected to 'the single-fixer roster (lead + one write-capable fixer + read-only analyst)'.

Files to Modify compacted from 10 lines to 3 (brace-grouped), with src/fixloop/ justified as a new flat src/ domain per R3 §9.1's observed convention — offsetting the AC additions to hold the story at exactly 200 lines.

surviving.summary: tests/backlog/keep-repoints.test.ts has no mirrored src/backlog/, a minor deviation from R3 §9.1's 'tests mirror source 1:1 at tests/<domain>/'. Harmless — the lint script already names `tests` so tooling scope is covered, and the test is a corpus regression check with no source domain by nature.

The escalation PR comment carries (error log, diff attempted, CI failure messages) with no explicit redaction clause. A provider auth error echoed from the box could in principle carry an LLM key fragment. Not fixed: the content originates in step output, which DF1.6 already covers via P1.6's verbatim-surviving INV-1 ('no secrets in step output'), so the chain is closed upstream; adding a second redaction rule here would duplicate an inherited invariant and expand scope.
